transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marta Alvarez (CTO - Cygnus), Samir Patel (ML Eng), Jordan Lee (Dev Lead)

Summary (auto): quick discovery focused on PLG quickstart, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated, security questions (SOC 2, VPC), and next steps for POC scoping.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE, and Priya is our systems engineer. Quick check on audio?
[00:18] Marta Alvarez: Sounds good, can hear you. Thanks Alex. We were excited to learn more about the PLG quickstart and how fast we can get up and running.
[00:30] Alex Chen: Great. Agenda — quick intro, you tell us what you're trying to solve, Priya will cover the quickstart & free credits, then we can dig into hosted vs dedicated and security.
[00:45] Priya Rao: Hi all. For context, quickstart is basically our self-serve flow: sign up, get free credits, run a few sample calls, and time-to-first-token is usually under a minute for simple text gen. Caveat: depends on model and region.
[01:10] Jordan Lee: Time-to-first-token under a minute, that's great. Our concern is latency at scale though; we do live features so p95 matters.
[01:28] Priya Rao: Totally. For PLG we recommend starting on Hosted API to validate, then consider Dedicated when you need predictable throughput. Hosted is easiest for quick wins and uses auto-routing.
[01:45] Samir Patel: What's the delta in cost and latency between hosted and dedicated? Any ballpark numbers?
[01:55] Alex Chen: Short answer: dedicated gives better p95 and cost predictability at scale because you reserve GPU capacity; hosted has flexibility and lower start-up friction. We'll send a spreadsheet with concrete numbers — rough thumb: dedicated can be 20-40% cheaper per token at sustained high throughput, but depends on model and batching.
[02:20] Marta Alvarez: And private/on-prem? We have some regulated customers asking for VPC or on-prem options.
[02:30] Priya Rao: Redwood Private supports VPC peering and an on-prem package. It integrates with KMS/HSM for encryption, and audit logs are baked in. On-prem has more ops work but meets compliance.
[02:48] Jordan Lee: How about SSO and RBAC? We use Okta.
[02:55] Alex Chen: We support SAML/Okta SSO and fine-grained RBAC. Also role-based API keys for service accounts.
[03:10] Samir Patel: Can you show the quickstart flow? We want to see time-to-first-token and SDK code.
[03:20] Priya Rao: Sure, I'll walk through steps. (screen share) First, sign up, redeem free credits, then in Console create an API key. Use our Python SDK or direct REST. Example code is three lines — instantiate client, call chat.create with prompt.
[03:45] Priya Rao: Note — if you're testing larger models, latency will rise; we have quantized variants and smaller models in the catalog for faster results. Also KV cache/prefix caching helps repeat prompts.
[04:10] Marta Alvarez: You said free credits — how much typically?
[04:16] Alex Chen: For PLG sign-ups we give starter credits that cover a few thousand tokens — enough to run quick tests and a basic demo. For pilots we often add extra credits.
[04:30] Jordan Lee: Are there any gotchas with billing when a team moves from hosted to dedicated? We want predictable invoices.
[04:40] Alex Chen: When you reserve Dedicated, billing switches to a commit (monthly/annual) and usage overage rules apply per contract. We'll map it during POC scoping so you can model costs.
[04:55] Samir Patel: Security: SOC 2 and audit logging — do you provide the reports and are they third-party?
[05:05] Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and can share the report under NDA. We also have ISO docs and detailed audit logs per request.
[05:20] Marta Alvarez: Great. On data residency — some EU customers require data to stay in EU. Any region controls?
[05:30] Alex Chen: You can pin region; Hosted supports region selection and Dedicated/Private can be deployed in specific regions. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated in-region or Private.
[05:45] Jordan Lee: Our main POC success criteria: (1) time-to-first-token < 60s for small models, (2) p95 latency < 500ms for small inputs in Dedicated, (3) ability to replay audit logs, and (4) clear migration path from hosted to dedicated.
[06:05] Alex Chen: Makes sense. We'll aim to validate those. For p95 we can run a benchmark — Priya can help with a config to reproduce your traffic pattern.
[06:20] Priya Rao: Yes, we'll provide a benchmark script (wrk-style) and a spreadsheet mapping model, batch size, and expected throughput.
[06:32] Samir Patel: One more question: are there restrictions on embeddings/PII? We need to know if data is used to train models.
[06:42] Alex Chen: Hosted API does not use customer data to train our models. For Dedicated/Private, data never leaves your environment. We'll include the exact data handling policy in the security packet.
[06:58] Marta Alvarez: Good. On integration, we have a containerized Python backend that will call Redwood. How do you handle SDK updates and breaking changes?
[07:10] Priya Rao: We maintain versioned SDKs and publish changelogs. For major breaking changes we give a migration window and deprecate old versions with notices. Console routes also show model migrations.
[07:30] Jordan Lee: Does Redwood support tool calling / function-calling patterns? We need structured outputs for follow-up actions.
[07:40] Priya Rao: Yes, function-calling and structured outputs are supported in the chat APIs; you can define schema and get deterministic JSON outputs. Works across hosted and dedicated.
[08:00] Samir Patel: Any examples of customers who started PLG and then moved to Dedicated? Curious about timeline.
[08:08] Alex Chen: Several — typical pattern is 2-3 months of PLG usage, then move to Dedicated when monthly QPS and p95 needs stabilize. We can share anonymized case studies.
[08:25] Marta Alvarez: We're also evaluating Anthropic and in-house inference. Main tradeoffs are safety and cost.
[08:33] Alex Chen: Understood. We can run comparative benchmarks if useful.
[08:40] Priya Rao: Also note that our Optimize tooling will recommend quantization profiles and batching for your workload to reduce unit cost without big quality loss.
[08:55] Jordan Lee: About latency at the edge — do you have edge regions or caching layers?
[09:05] Priya Rao: We have multi-region routing and prefix/KV cache. For very low latency edge needs we do dedicated edge nodes as part of Dedicated/Private deployments.
[09:25] Samir Patel: Let's talk about next steps — I'd like to try the time-to-first-token quickstart and then run a small load test.
[09:34] Alex Chen: Perfect. Next steps we'll do: send quickstart link & starter credits, Priya will share benchmark script and sample dedicated config, and schedule POC scoping for next week.
[09:48] Marta Alvarez: Sounds good. Can you also send SOC 2 redacted report?
[09:53] Alex Chen: Yes, will send SOC 2 under NDA.
[10:00] Jordan Lee: Any particular pitfalls to watch for when running the quickstart?
[10:06] Priya Rao: Just watch model choice and region. If you're on the free credits use a smaller model to validate. For prod-like tests use the benchmark config so you don't hit cold-start confusion. Also increase concurrency to exercise batching.
[10:28] Samir Patel: For the POC, we'd probably want a small dedicated pool for 2-3 weeks to validate p95 — is there a short-term commit option?
[10:36] Alex Chen: We have burst/dedicated pilot options for proof-of-value. We'll outline terms in the follow-up.
[10:46] Marta Alvarez: Who should I loop in for procurement and legal later?
[10:50] Alex Chen: I'll include our Sales Ops and Legal contacts in the email. For now, your procurement lead and security contact will be enough.
[11:00] Priya Rao: One minute on troubleshooting: if you hit latencies that look unexpected, send us request IDs and traces — Console has trace hooks. We'll correlate with our runtime logs.
[11:18] Jordan Lee: Good. Anything else?
[11:22] Alex Chen: I'll recap. Alex to send pricing deck, quickstart link, SOC 2 under NDA. Priya to send benchmark script and dedicated config. Customer to provision trial account and run time-to-first-token test. We'll set POC scoping for 2026-03-11.
[11:40] Marta Alvarez: Thanks, appreciate it.
[11:42] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email and drop the links.
[11:48] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: transcription includes minor mis-hears (e.g., K V cache sometimes transcribed as K-V cash), speaker overlaps. References: quickstart link (console.redwood.ai/quickstart), benchmark spreadsheet (link sent post-call), SOC 2 (NDA required).
